claim: The mushroom body (MB) is the center for associative learning in insects.
source: The mushroom body (MB) is the center for associative learning in insects.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in the field, supported by the citation to Davis, 2023 and other review articles.

claim: In Drosophila, intersectional split-GAL4 drivers and electron microscopy (EM) connectomes have laid the foundation for precise interrogation of the MB neural circuits.
source: In Drosophila, intersectional split-GAL4 drivers and electron microscopy (EM) connectomes have laid the foundation for precise interrogation of the MB neural circuits.
evidence: This statement is supported by the existence of these tools and their documented use in the field.

claim: Investigation of many cell types upstream and downstream of the MB has been hindered due to lack of specific driver lines.
source: However, investigation of many cell types upstream and downstream of the MB has been hindered due to lack of specific driver lines.
evidence: This is the motivation for the current study and is stated as a problem in the field.

claim: This study describes a new collection of over 800 split-GAL4 and split-LexA drivers that cover approximately 300 cell types.
source: Here we describe a new collection of over 800 split-GAL4 and split-LexA drivers that cover approximately 300 cell types, including sugar sensory neurons, putative nociceptive ascending neurons, olfactory and thermo-/hygro-sensory projection neurons, interneurons connected with the MB-extrinsic neurons, and various other cell types.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, directly stated in the abstract.

claim: The collection includes sugar sensory neurons, putative nociceptive ascending neurons, olfactory and thermo-/hygro-sensory projection neurons, interneurons connected with the MB-extrinsic neurons, and various other cell types.
source: Here we describe a new collection of over 800 split-GAL4 and split-LexA drivers that cover approximately 300 cell types, including sugar sensory neurons, putative nociceptive ascending neurons, olfactory and thermo-/hygro-sensory projection neurons, interneurons connected with the MB-extrinsic neurons, and various other cell types.
evidence: This is a description of the types of neurons covered by the driver collection.

claim: Activation phenotypes for a subset of these lines were characterized.
source: We characterized activation phenotypes for a subset of these lines and identified a sugar sensory neuron line most suitable for reward substitution.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the study.

claim: A sugar sensory neuron line most suitable for reward substitution was identified.
source: We characterized activation phenotypes for a subset of these lines and identified a sugar sensory neuron line most suitable for reward substitution.
evidence: This is a specific finding of the study.

claim: Neuronal morphological stereotypy was analyzed leveraging the thousands of confocal microscopy images associated with the collection.
source: Leveraging the thousands of confocal microscopy images associated with the collection, we analyzed neuronal morphological stereotypy and discovered that one set of mushroom body output neurons, MBON08/MBON09, exhibits striking individuality and asymmetry across animals.
evidence: This is a method and result described in the abstract.

claim: One set of mushroom body output neurons, MBON08/MBON09, exhibits striking individuality and asymmetry across animals.
source: Leveraging the thousands of confocal microscopy images associated with the collection, we analyzed neuronal morphological stereotypy and discovered that one set of mushroom body output neurons, MBON08/MBON09, exhibits striking individuality and asymmetry across animals.
evidence: This is a specific finding of the study.

claim: In conjunction with the EM connectome maps, the driver lines reported here offer a powerful resource for functional dissection of neural circuits for associative learning in adult Drosophila.
source: In conjunction with the EM connectome maps, the driver lines reported here offer a powerful resource for functional dissection of neural circuits for associative learning in adult Drosophila.
evidence: This is the conclusion and significance of the study.

claim: Approximately 2000 Kenyon cells (KCs), the MB's primary intrinsic neurons, represent the identity of sensory stimuli by their sparse activity patterns.
source: In Drosophila, approximately 2000 Kenyon cells (KCs), the MB's primary intrinsic neurons, represent the identity of sensory stimuli by their sparse activity patterns (Honegger et al., 2011; Perez-Orive et al., 2002; Turner et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a well-established fact in the field, supported by citations.

claim: Dopaminergic neurons (DANs) transmit signals related to the unconditioned stimulus (US), such as sugar rewards or electric shock punishments, to the MB.
source: Dopaminergic neurons (DANs) transmit signals related to the unconditioned stimulus (US), such as sugar rewards or electric shock punishments, to the MB (Burke et al., 2012; Kirkhart and Scott, 2015; Liu et al., 2012; Mao and Davis, 2009; Schwaerzel et al., 2003).
evidence: This is a well-established fact in the field, supported by citations.

claim: DANs and MB output neurons (MBONs) collectively form 15 compartmental zones that tile down the length of the KC axons in the MB lobes.
source: DANs and MB output neurons (MBONs) collectively form 15 compartmental zones that tile down the length of the KC axons in the MB lobes (Aso et al., 2014a; Tanaka et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a well-established fact in the field, supported by citations.

claim: Memories are stored as altered weights of synaptic connections between KCs and MB output neurons (MBONs) in each compartment.
source: Memories are stored as altered weights of synaptic connections between KCs and MB output neurons (MBONs) in each compartment (Hige et al., 2015a; Owald et al., 2015; Pai et al., 2013; Plaçais et al., 2013; Séjourné et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a well-established fact in the field, supported by citations.

claim: Relative activity levels of MBONs across compartments represent the valence of the learned CS and drive memory-based behaviors.
source: Relative activity levels of MBONs across compartments represent the valence of the learned CS and drive memory-based behaviors (Aso et al., 2014b; Owald et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a well-established fact in the field, supported by citations.

claim: The recently completed electron microscopy (EM) connectomes of the Drosophila brain in larvae and adults revealed thousands of interneurons upstream of DANs and downstream of MBONs.
source: The recently completed electron microscopy (EM) connectomes of the Drosophila brain in larvae and adults revealed thousands of interneurons upstream of DANs, which convey reinforcement signals to the MB, and downstream of MBONs, which link the MB to premotor pathways and other higher-order brain centers (Dorkenwald et al., 2023; Eichler et al., 2017; Eschbach et al., 2020; Hulse et al., 2021; Li et al., 2020; Scheffer et al., 2020; Winding et al., 2023; Zheng et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a recent finding in the field, supported by citations.

claim: Functional investigation of these interneuron cell types has been limited by the lack of cell-type-specific driver lines.
source: Functional investigation of these interneuron cell types has been limited by the lack of cell-type-specific driver lines.

claim: 93 split-GAL4 driver lines were previously generated that allowed for precise genetic access to 60 MB cell types.
source: Using the intersectional split-GAL4 method (Luan et al., 2020; Luan et al., 2006), we previously generated 93 split-GAL4 driver lines that allowed for precise genetic access to 60 MB cell types, including most of the KCs, DANs, MBONs and other modulatory neurons in the MB lobe regions (Aso et al., 2014a).
evidence: This is a statement about previous work by the authors.

Critically, a new collection of ZpGAL4DBD and p65ADZp hemidrivers became available (Dionne et al., 2018; Tirian and Dickson, 2017).

evidence: This is a statement about the uncertainty of the expression pattern.

claim: However it seems likely that the heterogeneity of Gr64f-Gal4 expression could limit its usage in generating fictive rewards in complex associative learning.
source: However it seems likely that the heterogeneity of Gr64f-Gal4 expression could limit its usage in generating fictive rewards in complex associative learning.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of Gr64f-Gal4.

claim: To refine Gr64f-Gal4 expression, we intersected Gr64f-GAL4DBD with various AD lines selected to have overlapping expression with a subset of the projection patterns of the original Gr64f-GAL4.
source: To refine Gr64f-Gal4 expression, we intersected Gr64f-GAL4DBD with various AD lines selected to have overlapping expression with a subset of the projection patterns of the original Gr64f-GAL4.
evidence: This is a description of the methods used in the study.

claim: We obtained 16 stable split-GAL4 lines with labeling in distinct subsets of the original expression pattern.
source: We obtained 16 stable split-GAL4 lines with labeling in distinct subsets of the original expression pattern (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: We examined the ability of these lines to serve as US in olfactory learning and their potency to drive local search behaviors, another memory-based behavior induced by appetitive stimuli.
source: We examined the ability of these lines to serve as US in olfactory learning (Aso and Rubin, 2016) and their potency to drive local search behaviors, another memory-based behavior induced by appetitive stimuli (Corfas et al., 2019; Figure 8, Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a description of the methods used in the study.

claim: Additionally, we measured the walking speed of flies, as flies decrease walking while feeding.
source: Additionally, we measured the walking speed of flies, as flies decrease walking while feeding (Thoma et al., 2016; Aso and Rubin, 2016).
evidence: This is a description of the methods used in the study, supported by citations.

claim: Among the Gr64f-split-GAL4 lines, SS87269 emerged as the best driver for substituting sugar reward in olfactory learning given its anatomical specificity as well as its effectiveness throughout long training protocols.
source: Among the Gr64f-split-GAL4 lines, SS87269 emerged as the best driver for substituting sugar reward in olfactory learning given its anatomical specificity as well as its effectiveness throughout long training protocols (Figure 8E).
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: SS87269 expresses in the labellum and in at least two types of tarsal sensory neurons, namely the ascending (atGRN) and the non-ascending segment-specific (stGRN) types.
source: SS87269 expresses in the labellum and in at least two types of tarsal sensory neurons, namely the ascending (atGRN) and the non-ascending segment-specific (stGRN) types (Figure 7E and F).
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: The driver does not label pharyngeal sensory neurons, and importantly, it lacks expression in abdominal ganglion and olfactory sensory neurons, which could reflect off-target expression from the original Gr64f-GAL4.
source: The driver does not label pharyngeal sensory neurons, and importantly, it lacks expression in abdominal ganglion and olfactory sensory neurons, which could reflect off-target expression from the original Gr64f-GAL4.
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: When odor presentation was paired with the activation of SS87269 neurons, flies formed robust appetitive memories even after extended training with high LED intensity.
source: When odor presentation was paired with the activation of SS87269 neurons, flies formed robust appetitive memories even after extended training with high LED intensity (Figure 8E, Figure 8—figure supplement 1 and Video 1).
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: Furthermore, and consistent with the idea that this subset of sensory neurons encodes appetitive food-related taste information, activating these neurons elicited proboscis extension and slowed flies.
source: Furthermore, and consistent with the idea that this subset of sensory neurons encodes appetitive food-related taste information, activating these neurons elicited proboscis extension and slowed flies (Figure 8F–I; Figure 8—figure supplement 2, Video 2 and Video 3).
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: These flies also showed robust local search behavior during the post-activation period, that is an increased probability of revisiting the area where they experienced the activation.
source: These flies also showed robust local search behavior during the post-activation period, that is an increased probability of revisiting the area where they experienced the activation (Video 4).
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: Notably, the revisiting phenotype of SS87269 was stronger than any other Gr64f-split-GAL4 drivers and the original Gr64f-GAL4 even after 180 repetitive activation trials.
source: Notably, the revisiting phenotype of SS87269 was stronger than any other Gr64f-split-GAL4 drivers (Figure 8, Figure 8—figure supplement 2Figure 8F, Figure 8—figure supplement 2A) and the original Gr64f-GAL4 even after 180 repetitive activation trials (Figure 8—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: Two other lines SS88801 and SS88776, which label stGRNs or stGRNs along with labial sensory neurons, respectively, similarly showed appetitive learning and reduced locomotion during activation.
source: Two other lines SS88801 and SS88776, which label stGRNs or stGRNs along with labial sensory neurons, respectively (Figure 7K–L and I), similarly showed appetitive learning and reduced locomotion during activation (Figure 8E–F).
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: Interestingly, however, the activation of stGRNs with SS88801 did not induce significant local search behaviors.
source: Interestingly, however, the activation of stGRNs with SS88801 did not induce significant local search behaviors (Figure 8F, Figure 8—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: This finding could be valuable for understanding circuits underlying local search behavior and invites further investigation to compare pathways from labial and tarsal sensory neurons to the MB and the central complex.
source: This finding could be valuable for understanding circuits underlying local search behavior and invites further investigation to compare pathways from labial and tarsal sensory neurons to the MB and the central complex.
evidence: This is a statement about the significance of the finding.

claim: In contrast to SS87269, two other lines, SS87278 and SS87279, express in cells that appear to convey aversive signals.
source: In contrast to SS87269, two other lines, SS87278 and SS87279, express in cells that appear to convey aversive signals.
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: Activation of these lines induced an increase in walking speed during activation and reduced the probability of revisiting where flies received activation LED light.
source: Activation of these lines induced an increase in walking speed during activation and reduced the probability of revisiting where flies received activation LED light (Figure 8F, Figure 8—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: Also, flies became progressively less mobile during the inter-trial interval period.
source: Also, flies became progressively less mobile during the inter-trial interval period (Figure 8G).
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: We made a similar observation with the original Gr64f-GAL4 as well as with a bitter-taste driver, Gr66a-GAL4.
source: We made a similar observation with the original Gr64f-GAL4 (Figure 8G) as well as with a bitter-taste driver, Gr66a-GAL4 (data not shown).
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: With extended training using SS87278 and SS87279, the preference to the paired odor eventually became negative.
source: With extended training using SS87278 and SS87279, the preference to the paired odor eventually became negative (Figure 8E).
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: These drivers label distinct subsets of sensory neurons projecting to the abdominal ganglion.
source: These drivers label distinct subsets of sensory neurons projecting to the abdominal ganglion (Figure 7O and P).
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: The innervation of SS87278 inside the abdominal ganglion is similar to that of Gr66a-GAL4, which is known to label multidendritic sensory neurons in the adult Drosophila abdomen.
source: The innervation of SS87278 inside the abdominal ganglion is similar to that of Gr66a-GAL4 (Figure 7Q; Dunipace et al., 2001), which is known to label multidendritic sensory neurons in the adult Drosophila abdomen (Shimono et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a result of the study, supported by citations.

claim: Examining projection patterns in fly bodies with whole-animal agar sections, we found that sensory neurons in SS87278 also project to the abdominal body surface, likely representing the class IV multidendritic neurons that detect multimodal nociceptive stimuli.
source: Examining projection patterns in fly bodies with whole-animal agar sections, we found that sensory neurons in SS87278 also project to the abdominal body surface (Figure 7J), likely representing the class IV multidendritic neurons that detect multimodal nociceptive stimuli (Hwang et al., 2007; Ohyama et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a result of the study, supported by citations.

claim: The expression in these aversive sensory neurons therefore may complicate the interpretation of appetitive learning with the original Gr64f-GAL4.
source: The expression in these aversive sensory neurons therefore may complicate the interpretation of appetitive learning with the original Gr64f-GAL4.
evidence: This is a statement about the implications of the finding.

claim: Overall, the refinement of Gr64f-Gal4 expression with SS87269 now allows for specific manipulation of the rewarding subset of gustatory sensory neurons and permits training with an extended number of trials.
source: Overall, the refinement of Gr64f-Gal4 expression with SS87269 now allows for specific manipulation of the rewarding subset of gustatory sensory neurons and permits training with an extended number of trials.
evidence: This is a statement about the significance of the finding.

claim: While we have not yet conducted extensive anatomical screening, LexADBD lines generated with Gr64f, Gr43a, Gr66a, Gr28b.d promoters should allow for comparable refinement of driver lines to target sensory neurons expressing these receptors.
source: While we have not yet conducted extensive anatomical screening, LexADBD lines generated with Gr64f, Gr43a, Gr66a, Gr28b.d promoters (Figure 7A) should allow for comparable refinement of driver lines to target sensory neurons expressing these receptors.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential of the new lines.

claim: For instance, we generated split-LexA drivers specific for internal fructose sensory neurons or a subset of bitter taste neurons.
source: For instance, we generated split-LexA drivers specific for internal fructose sensory neurons (Miyamoto et al., 2012) or a subset of bitter taste neurons (Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a result of the study, supported by a citation.

claim: We also made a small number of lines for cell types in the subesophageal zone (SEZ) area, which complement previous collections of drivers for gustatory interneurons.
source: We also made a small number of lines for cell types in the subesophageal zone (SEZ) area (Figure 7—figure supplement 3), which complement previous collections of drivers for gustatory interneurons (Otto et al., 2020; Sterne et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a result of the study, supported by citations.

claim: Lastly, we generated driver lines for putative ascending nociceptive pathways.
source: Lastly, we generated driver lines for putative ascending nociceptive pathways.
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: We tested whether optogenetic activation would drive avoidance related behaviors using the circular arena, where an activating LED illuminated two quadrants of the arena, and the other two remained dark.
source: We tested whether optogenetic activation would drive avoidance related behaviors using the circular arena, where an activating LED illuminated two quadrants of the arena, and the other two remained dark.
evidence: This is a description of the methods used in the study.

claim: We determined the quadrant preference for 581 combinations of ZpGAL4DBD and p65ADZp hemidrivers.
source: We determined the quadrant preference for 581 combinations of ZpGAL4DBD and p65ADZp hemidrivers.
evidence: This is a description of the methods used in the study.

claim: We found one driver, SS01159, which showed the most robust avoidance of the illuminated quadrants, and exhibited behavioral features characteristic of nociception, including backward walking, turning, increased speed, and jumping upon activation.
source: We found one driver, SS01159, which showed the most robust avoidance of the illuminated quadrants, and exhibited behavioral features characteristic of nociception, including backward walking, turning, increased speed, and jumping upon activation (Figure 9B–D, and Video 5).
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: This driver labels a group of ascending neurons, which likely carry nociceptive signals from the body and legs to the brain.
source: This driver labels a group of ascending neurons (Figure 9E), which likely carry nociceptive signals from the body and legs to the brain.
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: We then generated drivers for subsets of these ascending neurons guided by single neuron morphologies of cells in SS01159 determined by MCFO stochastic labeling.
source: We then generated drivers for subsets of these ascending neurons guided by single neuron morphologies of cells in SS01159 determined by MCFO stochastic labeling (Nern et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a description of the methods used in the study, supported by a citation.

claim: While not completely matched to EM cell types due to only a portion of their morphologies being available in the hemibrain volume, these lines serve as a valuable resource for querying the reinforcement pathways.
source: While not completely matched to EM cell types due to only a portion of their morphologies being available in the hemibrain volume, these lines serve as a valuable resource for querying the reinforcement pathways.
evidence: This is a statement about the utility of the lines.

claim: Neuronal morphology can vary, and the randomness of developmental processes can ultimately result in differences in behavior among individuals.
source: Neuronal morphology can vary, and the randomness of developmental processes can ultimately result in differences in behavior among individuals (Linneweber).
evidence: This is a statement about the field, supported by a citation.

claim: The recent landmark study systematically examined morphological variability of neurons using the EM connectomic data.
source: The recent landmark study systematically examined morphological variability of neurons using the EM connectomic data (Schlegel et al., 2023), but it will only be possible to examine relatively few individual brains for the foreseeable future.
evidence: This is a statement about a recent study, supported by a citation.

claim: As a part of Janelia Flylight team project to generate cell-type-specific driver lines, we have imaged over 6,000 fly brains for the present study.
source: As a part of Janelia Flylight team project to generate cell-type-specific driver lines, we have imaged over 6,000 fly brains for the present study.
evidence: This is a statement about the data collected in the study.

claim: While annotating those confocal images, we occasionally encountered samples with atypical morphologies.
source: While annotating those confocal images, we occasionally encountered samples with atypical morphologies (Figure 10).
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: For example, one V_l2PN neuron, which typically projects to the lateral horn of the ipsilateral hemisphere, exhibited a peculiar morphology in one brain sample, where its axon crossed the midline and projected to the contralateral hemisphere, yet it still reached the correct target area within the lateral horn of the opposite side.
source: For example, one V_l2PN neuron, which typically projects to the lateral horn of the ipsilateral hemisphere, exhibited a peculiar morphology in one brain sample, where its axon crossed the midline and projected to the contralateral hemisphere, yet it still reached the correct target area within the lateral horn of the opposite side (Figure 10A).
evidence: This is a specific example of atypical morphology.

claim: Another instance involved a DPM neuron, the sole serotonergic neuron of the MB lobes. While typical brain samples contain only one DPM neuron per hemisphere, we found a brain with two DPM neurons in one hemisphere.
source: Another instance involved a DPM neuron, the sole serotonergic neuron of the MB lobes. While typical brain samples contain only one DPM neuron per hemisphere, we found a brain with two DPM neurons in one hemisphere (Figure 10B).
evidence: This is a specific example of atypical morphology.

claim: In this case, the DPM projections exhibited an atypical innervation of the calyx of the mushroom body.
source: In this case, the DPM projections exhibited an atypical innervation of the calyx of the mushroom body.
evidence: This is a specific example of atypical morphology.

claim: We also found examples involving MBONs. The dendrites of MBON-α1 are typically confined to the α lobe of the MB, but we discovered a case where this cell in addition sent projections to the ellipsoid body.
source: We also found examples involving MBONs. The dendrites of MBON-α1 are typically confined to the α lobe of the MB, but we discovered a case where this cell in addition sent projections to the ellipsoid body (Figure 10C).
evidence: This is a specific example of atypical morphology.

claim: MBON-α3 displayed striking variability in soma positions, but only subtle variability in axonal projections.
source: MBON-α3 displayed striking variability in soma positions, but only subtle variability in axonal projections (Figure 10D).
evidence: This is a specific example of atypical morphology.

claim: Overall in 1241 brain hemispheres examined, we found mislocalization of dendrites and axons in 3.14% and 0.97% of MB cell types, respectively.
source: Overall in 1241 brain hemispheres examined, we found mislocalization of dendrites and axons in 3.14% and 0.97% of MB cell types, respectively.
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: If this rate of mislocalization is generalizable to other brain regions, a fly brain of ~130,000 neurons would have a few thousands of neurons with mislocalized dendrites or axons.
source: If this rate of mislocalization is generalizable to other brain regions, a fly brain of ~130,000 neurons (Dorkenwald et al., 2023) would have a few thousands of neurons with mislocalized dendrites or axons.
evidence: This is an extrapolation from the data, supported by a citation.

claim: These examples of atypical morphology were observed only once in dozens of samples, and thus can be considered as erroneous projections either resulting from stochastic developmental processes, or possibly caused by ectopic expression of reporter proteins on the plasma membrane at a high level.
source: These examples of atypical morphology were observed only once in dozens of samples, and thus can be considered as erroneous projections either resulting from stochastic developmental processes, or possibly caused by ectopic expression of reporter proteins on the plasma membrane at a high level.
evidence: This is a statement about the interpretation of the findings.

claim: In contrast to these rare, and seemingly erroneous, morphological variations, we observed much more frequent and reproducible variations in the composition as well as morphologies in the two MBONs (MBON08 and MBON09) labeled by MB083C, which may amount to 'individuality'.
source: In contrast to these rare, and seemingly erroneous, morphological variations, we observed much more frequent and reproducible variations in the composition as well as morphologies in the two MBONs (MBON08 and MBON09) labeled by MB083C, which may amount to 'individuality'.
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: This split-GAL4 driver line invariably labels two cells in each hemisphere in 169 brain samples examined with four different reporters and in both sexes.
source: This split-GAL4 driver line invariably labels two cells in each hemisphere in 169 brain samples examined with four different reporters and in both sexes (57 males and 112 females; Figure 11—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: In all samples, these MBONs arborize dendrites in the γ3 and β′1 compartments.
source: In all samples, these MBONs arborize dendrites in the γ3 and β′1 compartments.
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: An obvious mistargeting of the axon was observed in only one sample, suggesting highly consistent development of these MBONs.
source: An obvious mistargeting of the axon was observed in only one sample, suggesting highly consistent development of these MBONs (Figure 11A and B).
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: However, MCFO method visualized two distinct morphologies of these MBONs: MBON08 arborizes dendrites in the γ3 compartment of both hemispheres, whereas MBON09 arborize dendrites in ipsilateral γ3 and contralateral β′1.
source: However, MCFO method visualized two distinct morphologies of these MBONs: MBON08 arborizes dendrites in the γ3 compartment of both hemispheres, whereas MBON09 arborize dendrites in ipsilateral γ3 and contralateral β′1 (Figure 11C–H; Aso et al., 2014a).
evidence: This is a result of the study, supported by a citation.

claim: β′1 compartment was always labeled in both hemispheres for all 169 samples, suggesting that MBON09 represents at least one of the two cells in each hemisphere.
source: β′1 compartment was always labeled in both hemispheres for all 169 samples, suggesting that MBON09 represents at least one of the two cells in each hemisphere.
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: The second cell can be either MBON08 or MBON09.
source: The second cell can be either MBON08 or MBON09.
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: In MCFO experiments, we observed 21 instances of MBON08 (8 in the left and 13 in the right hemisphere) and 188 instances of MBON09.
source: In MCFO experiments, we observed 21 instances of MBON08 (8 in the left and 13 in the right hemisphere) and 188 instances of MBON09 (Figure 11I).
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: Based on these observations, we expect 65% of flies contain four MBON09, while the remaining 35% of flies likely have at least one MBON08.
source: Based on these observations, we expect 65% of flies contain four MBON09, while the remaining 35% of flies likely have at least one MBON08 (Figure 11J).
evidence: This is an inference from the data.

claim: In 71 hemispheres, two cells were visualized in different colors of MCFO: 52 contained two MBON09 and 19 contained one MBON08 and MBON09.
source: In 71 hemispheres, two cells were visualized in different colors of MCFO: 52 contained two MBON09 and 19 contained one MBON08 and MBON09.
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: We never observed a brain with MBON08 on both hemispheres or two MBON08 in one hemisphere.
source: We never observed a brain with MBON08 on both hemispheres or two MBON08 in one hemisphere (Figure 11J).
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: When MBON08 and MBON09 coexist, MBON09 arborized in the lateral part of the ipsilateral γ3 and MBON08 arborize in the medial part of the contralateral γ3.
source: When MBON08 and MBON09 coexist, MBON09 arborized in the lateral part of the ipsilateral γ3 and MBON08 arborize in the medial part of the contralateral γ3 (Figure 11E–H).
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: This seemingly extended γ3 compartment innervated by MBON08 is not part of γ4, because it did not overlap with DANs in the γ4.
source: This seemingly extended γ3 compartment innervated by MBON08 is not part of γ4, because it did not overlap with DANs in the γ4 (Figure 11—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: Although MBON08 was not found in brain samples used for the hemibrain or FAFB EM connectome, DANs in the γ3 could be subdivided to two groups that innervate the medial or lateral part of the γ3.
source: Although MBON08 was not found in brain samples used for the hemibrain or FAFB EM connectome (Dorkenwald et al., 2023; Scheffer et al., 2020; Zheng et al., 2018), DANs in the γ3 could be subdivided to two groups that innervate the medial or lateral part of the γ3 (Figure 11—figure supplement 2C; Li et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a result of the study, supported by citations.

claim: Therefore, subdivision of the γ3 compartment may exist irrespective of heterogeneity on the MBON side.
source: Therefore, subdivision of the γ3 compartment may exist irrespective of heterogeneity on the MBON side.
evidence: This is an inference from the data.

claim: In larval brains, two MBONs that correspond to adult MBON08/09 exhibit identical morphology.
source: In larval brains, two MBONs that correspond to adult MBON08/09 exhibit identical morphology (Eichler et al., 2017; Saumweber et al., 2018; Truman et al., 2023).
evidence: This is a statement about larval brains, supported by citations.

claim: During metamorphosis, these larval MBONs may acquire distinct morphology as MBON08 at 21/209 odds.
source: During metamorphosis, these larval MBONs may acquire distinct morphology as MBON08 at 21/209 odds.
evidence: This is an inference from the data.

claim: We have never observed a brain with MBON08 on both hemispheres, and therefore MBON08 is likely to appear in only one hemisphere, if at all.
source: We have never observed a brain with MBON08 on both hemispheres, and therefore MBON08 is likely to appear in only one hemisphere, if at all (Figure 11J).
evidence: This is an inference from the data.

claim: This resulting asymmetry could be one source of turning handedness and idiosyncratic learning performance, given that MBON09 forms extensive connections with other MBONs and fan-shaped body neurons and the activity of MBON08/MBON09 has a strong influence on turning.
source: This resulting asymmetry could be one source of turning handedness and idiosyncratic learning performance (de Bivort et al., 2022; Smith et al., 2022), given that MBON09 forms extensive connections with other MBONs and fan-shaped body neurons (Hulse et al., 2021; Li et al., 2020) and the activity of MBON08/MBON09 has a strong influence on turning (Aso et al., 2023; Matheson et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a statement about the potential implications of the finding, supported by citations.

claim: Split-GAL4 lines can be converted into split-LexA lines by replacing the GAL4 DNA binding domain with that of LexA.
source: Split-GAL4 lines can be converted into split-LexA lines by replacing the GAL4 DNA binding domain with that of LexA (Ting et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a statement about a method, supported by a citation.

claim: To broaden the utility of the split-GAL4 lines that have been frequently used since the publication in 2014, we have generated over 20 LexADBD lines to test the conversions of split-GAL4 to split-LexA.
source: To broaden the utility of the split-GAL4 lines that have been frequently used since the publication in 2014 (Aso et al., 2014a), we have generated over 20 LexADBD lines to test the conversions of split-GAL4 to split-LexA.
evidence: This is a description of the methods used in the study, supported by a citation.

claim: The majority (22 out of 34) of the resulting split-LexA lines exhibited very similar expression patterns to their corresponding original split-GAL4 lines.
source: The majority (22 out of 34) of the resulting split-LexA lines exhibited very similar expression patterns to their corresponding original split-GAL4 lines (Figure 12).
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: The main mode of failure when converting to LexA was that expression levels become too weak and stochastic.
source: The main mode of failure when converting to LexA was that expression levels become too weak and stochastic.
evidence: This is a result of the study.

claim: The ability to define and manipulate a small group of neurons is crucial for studying neural circuits.
source: The ability to define and manipulate a small group of neurons is crucial for studying neural circuits.
evidence: This is a statement about the importance of the work.

claim: Here, we have generated and characterized driver lines targeting specific cell types that are likely to be a part of associative learning circuits centered on the MB.
source: Here, we have generated and characterized driver lines targeting specific cell types that are likely to be a part of associative learning circuits centered on the MB.
evidence: This is a summary of the work.

claim: We have provided these driver lines with a comprehensive lookup table linking these cell types with the EM hemibrain connectome.
source: We have provided these driver lines with a comprehensive lookup table linking these cell types with the EM hemibrain connectome (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a summary of the work.

claim: These lines, together with preceding collections of drivers, collectively constitute a powerful resource for precise functional interrogation of associative learning in adult Drosophila melanogaster, and will be a foundation to reveal conserved principles of neural circuits for associative learning.
source: These lines, together with preceding collections of drivers (Aso et al., 2014a; Aso and Rubin, 2016; Davis et al., 2020; Dolan et al., 2018; Rubin and Aso, 2024; Shuai et al., 2015; see for examples: Sterne et al., 2021; Strother et al., 2017; Truman et al., 2023; Tuthill et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2021; Wolff and Rubin, 2018; Wu et al., 2016), collectively constitute a powerful resource for precise functional interrogation of associative learning in adult Drosophila melanogaster, and will be a foundation to reveal conserved principles of neural circuits for associative learning.
evidence: This is a statement about the significance of the work, supported by citations.
